reason: Keep the action, but the finding's reasoning is backwards. Scores only rise, so a newer S0 has MORE teams above us, not fewer. A stale S0 can therefore miss an UP and give a false '0', and '0' is the only code that closes the CI/SEC levers. Nothing guaranteed that '0 passed stays 0'. The code-0 result is correct only because I checked it directly. Against S1 = ladder_watch/20260927T222653Z (#165, count 48, k=8), 0 TeamIds passed for every count-47 S0: 185549Z (#162, k=11), e10 2002Z (k=10), 2043Z (k=9), and 2143Z (the newest count-47 download, #163, k=8). The 46 read broke the R19-A1 (1) text in two ways: it did not use the newest count-47 S0, and it did not log k. k at its actual S0 was 11, not 10. k=10 at 20:02Z is already logged in R20-A2 (1). k=8 at 22:30Z is confirmed (e10 2230Z l.996: pos 9 of 52; 2243Z still 8). k fell 11 -> 8 from 18:55Z to 21:43Z, then held flat. BLIND is a real risk by the ~07:30-08:00Z cap reads, but not imminent. The change only adds logging: no submit, no new mechanism, R1-R10 unaffected, zero runtime.
fix: Append to CONTEXT: '46 read addendum: R19-A1 (1) S0 should have been the newest count-47 download = e10_watch/20260927T2143Z.txt (#163, k=8). Re-run vs S1 ladder_watch/20260927T222653Z (#165, count 48, k=8): 0 passed. Also 0 passed from 185549Z (k=11), 2002Z (k=10) and 2043Z (k=9). Code 0 stands. k at 22:30Z/22:43Z = 8.' For W1, S0 = the newest download showing the count just before that file scores (48 for the first W1 completion, then 49, 50 ...; each S1 becomes the next S0). It is not always count 48. Take a fresh manual download near each expected completion so S0 is as late as possible. Log k, and k = 0 -> BLIND '?'. Drop the finding's clause 'other teams only rise, so 0 stays 0'.
realistic_gain: No direct LB or private gain. This is process hygiene. It prevents a false '0' that would close CI/SEC from a stale S0, and it gives an auditable k/BLIND log for W1/W2. Cost: about 5 min of logging.
